name: Cape Town
tagline: Africa's best restaurant in a treehouse over the vineyards, and the gatsby that feeds four people.

La Colombe.description: Franco-Asian fusion in a treehouse over the Silvermist estate. Africa's best restaurant, among the world's top 50.

Mariam's Kitchen.description: Cape Town's most famous steak-and-masala gatsby, an urban classic since 1985.

FYN Restaurant.description: South African cuisine with Japanese technique from chef Peter Tempelhoff, a regular on The World's 50 Best Restaurants list.

Biesmiellah.description: Halal Cape Malay cuisine in the colorful heart of Bo-Kaap, run by the Osman family for more than four decades.

Kalky's.description: A fish-and-chips shack by the Kalk Bay fishing harbor, with the freshest fish on the peninsula.

Wolfgat.description: A tiny 20-seat restaurant beside a coastal cave in Paternoster; named Best Restaurant in Africa at The World's 50 Best Restaurants 2021, with hyperlocal west-coast cooking from chef Kobus van der Merwe.

Foxcroft.description: Relaxed fine dining in Constantia from chef Scot Kirton of the La Colombe group; winner of the Eat Out New Restaurant award and a repeat Restaurant of the Year nominee.

Chef's Warehouse at Beau Constantia.description: A tasting menu with views over the Constantia wine valley, led by chef Ivor Jones (formerly of The Test Kitchen and La Colombe) at the Beau Constantia estate.

The Pot Luck Club.description: A tapas restaurant inside a converted grain silo at Woodstock's Old Biscuit Mill, created by acclaimed chef Luke Dale-Roberts (The Test Kitchen).

The Shortmarket Club.description: A European-style bistro in the heart of the CBD, another Luke Dale-Roberts project, serving reinvented classics with an acclaimed wine list.

Belly of the Beast.description: A seasonal restaurant in the East City led by chef Odette Olivier, focused on local ingredients and fermentation; featured on the World's 50 Best discovery list.

Chef's Warehouse & Canteen.description: Globally inspired small-plates cooking on Bree Street from chef Liam Tomlin, with an ever-changing shared menu and one of the city centre's most talked-about wine cellars.

95 Keerom.description: Northern Italian cooking from Milanese chef Giorgio Nava, in a heritage building that once housed the Company's Garden stables; regarded as one of the best Italian restaurants outside Italy.

Societi Bistro.description: A classic bistro in a Georgian house in Gardens, serving comforting French bistro staples with an extensive by-the-glass wine list.

Grub & Vine.description: Honest bistro cooking and a carefully chosen wine list in a heritage building on Bree Street, from chef Matt Manning.

Kloof Street House.description: A Victorian house set in a tree-lined garden on Kloof Street, famous for its gatsby sandwich and Gatsby-era atmosphere; part restaurant, part bar, part beer garden.

La Tête.description: Nose-to-tail cooking from brothers Giles and James Edwards on Bree Street, built on using the whole animal and direct relationships with producers.

Willoughby & Co.description: A sushi and seafood counter at the V&A Waterfront since 1996, famous for its long queues and the complimentary glass of wine while you wait.

Harbour House.description: A seafood restaurant overlooking the Victoria Basin at the V&A Waterfront, a Cape Town classic for a harbourside lunch.

Baia Seafood Restaurant.description: Seafood with panoramic harbour views since 2001, known for its Portuguese-inspired cataplana at the V&A Waterfront.

The Codfather.description: Fresh fish and sushi displayed on ice for guests to choose before it's cooked, a casual Camps Bay classic.

The Foodbarn.description: Bistronomy and tapas cooking from chef Franck Dangereux, a pioneer of Cape Town fine dining (founder of the original La Colombe), in laid-back Noordhoek Farm Village.

Africa Café.description: One of South Africa's first pan-African restaurants, opened in 1992 by chef Portia Mbau; a tasting menu of dishes from across the continent.

Mama Africa.description: A pan-African restaurant on Long Street since 1995, with live marimba bands every night and a mixed grill of crocodile, ostrich and kudu.

Gold Restaurant.description: A pan-African dining experience in a converted De Waterkant warehouse, with djembe drumming, dance and a fourteen-course menu from across the continent.

Bo-Kaap Kombuis.description: Traditional Cape Malay cooking in a family home on the slopes of Signal Hill with views of Table Mountain; Michelin-starred chefs have come to learn from owner Nazli Larney.

Atlas Trading Company.description: Bo-Kaap's oldest spice shop, founded in 1946 by the Ahmed family; the go-to source for Cape Malay and curry spice blends.

Hussar Grill Rondebosch.description: A South African grill founded in 1964 in Rondebosch by Allen Ambor, a pioneer of the local steakhouse and now a citywide chain.

Beefcakes.description: A kitsch burger joint with live drag shows in Green Point, a gay-friendly icon of Cape Town nightlife.

Royale Eatery.description: A pioneering gourmet burger joint on Long Street, with more than 50 burger varieties and hand-spun milkshakes.

Truth Coffee Roasting.description: A steampunk-styled coffee roastery in a Victorian warehouse; named 'World's Best Coffee Shop' by the UK's Daily Telegraph two years running.

Origin Coffee Roasting.description: One of the pioneers of Cape Town's specialty coffee scene, housed in an industrial warehouse in De Waterkant.

Jason Bakery.description: A go-to Green Point bakery famous for its croissants; founder Jason Lillie is known as Cape Town's croissant king.

Charly's Bakery.description: A colorful family-run bakery in Zonnebloem known for its whimsical cakes, star of the South African docu-series 'Charly's Cake Angels', broadcast in over 100 countries.

Neighbourgoods Market.description: The Saturday market that launched Cape Town's 'hipster' food scene in 2006, inside Woodstock's historic Old Biscuit Mill, with dozens of street-food stalls.

Oranjezicht City Farm Market.description: A producers' market that grew out of a community urban farm founded in 2012, now held by the V&A Waterfront, with over 40 farmers and 80 artisanal food traders.

Bay Harbour Market.description: An indoor market at the Hout Bay fishing harbour, with food stalls, crafts and live music on weekends.

Buitenverwachting.description: The restaurant of the historic Buitenverwachting wine estate, whose origins date to the late 17th century, in the Constantia valley.

Jonkershuis at Groot Constantia.description: A Cape Malay-influenced bistro beside the manor house at Groot Constantia, South Africa's oldest wine estate, beneath centuries-old oaks.

La Petite Colombe.description: La Colombe's sister restaurant in Franschhoek, on the Leeu Estates farm; French-South African fine dining among the vines, featured on the World's 50 Best discovery list.
